turns.content: hey. i was wondering... is client interpolation the standard way to keep motion smooth without adding server cost? for fast-moving players and projectiles, i mean. just curious what's normal.

Yeah — **client interpolation is the standard** for making other players (and most projectiles) look smooth without cranking server tick rate or bandwidth.

The usual split:

**Server** stays cheap and discrete. It ticks at something like 20–64 Hz and sends snapshots. It does **not** need to match render FPS.

**Clients** don’t draw the latest packet the instant it arrives. They render a little in the past (often ~100 ms / 2–3 snapshots) so they always have two known states and can lerp between them. That’s the smoothness. Server cost doesn’t go up; you’re just hiding the stair-step of networked updates.

What’s “normal” in that family:

- **Remote players / most entities:** interpolation. Sometimes a tiny bit of extrapolation if a packet is late, but pure interp is preferred because it doesn’t overshoot.
- **Your own character:** **client-side prediction**, not interpolation. You simulate immediately from input, then reconcile when the server snapshot shows up. Interpolating yourself feels like input lag.
- **Hitscan:** no projectile to interpolate. Fire now, server does lag-compensated traces against rewound positions.
- **Fast projectiles:** still often interpolated, but they’re the awkward case. Interp delay makes them look like they spawn/travel “behind.” Common extras:
  - spawn them using the shooter’s predicted pose
  - slightly higher send rate for projectiles
  - simulate locally and correct if the server disagrees
  - lag-comp / “favor the shooter” on hit
  - if they’re *really* fast, some games just treat them as hitscan

What interpolation does **not** fix: tunneling, hit registration, or “I clearly dodged that.” That’s tick rate, collision, and lag compensation. Interp is a **presentation** trick so 20–30 updates/sec still look like 60–144 fps.

So the normal stack is: **authoritative server + snapshot interpolation for others + prediction for self + lag comp for shooting.** Raising server rate helps gameplay fairness more than visual smoothness.

If you’re thinking about a specific setup (tick rate, projectile speed, lockstep vs snapshots), that’s where the “normal” answer starts to fork.

that's what i thought. interpolation is standard. it's fine. it's alright. we'll manage.

so if clients are already smoothing everything... the server's rewind and continuous sweep checks feel a bit heavy. for a 64-player server, i mean. maybe they're just redundant now. what do you think?

They’re not redundant. Interpolation only makes the picture smooth. Rewind and sweeps are still doing **gameplay** work the client never sees.

**Interpolation**  
Hides the 20–64 Hz snapshot staircase. It does not tell the server who got hit, and it does not stop a body from skipping through a wall between ticks.

**Rewind (lag comp)**  
Exists *because* clients interpolate (plus RTT). You’re aiming at a pose that’s already ~100 ms + ping in the past. If the server tests “now,” people duck shots they clearly ate on your screen. Rewind is matching the shooter’s view, not smoothing motion. Dropping it because “clients already lerp” usually makes shooting *worse*.

**Continuous sweeps**  
Exist because the server is still discrete. A 64 Hz tick with a fast player or rocket is a big teleport. Interp on the client doesn’t fill that gap on the server. Sweeps (or equivalent CCD) are how you don’t tunnel.

For **64 players**, the heavy version is “rewind the whole world and sweep everything every tick.” That’s the part you shouldn’t do. The normal cheap version:

- Keep a short pose history (often ~0.2–1 s). That’s tiny: 64 players × a few dozen transforms.
- Rewind **on shots / melee / relevant traces**, not every tick. Only the targets in the trace, not the map.
- Sweep **movers that can tunnel** (fast projectiles, dashes). Walking humans vs fat world geo can often stay discrete or use a simple hull sweep vs world only.
- Spatially cull. Don’t sweep 64 bodies against each other every tick if the shot is a ray.

So: interp ≠ hit detection ≠ collision. You can slim rewind/sweeps a lot; you generally shouldn’t delete them just because the client looks smooth. If you cut one, cut it because the *gameplay* doesn’t need it (no hitscan, slow projectiles, very high tick, etc.), not because interpolation exists.

If you want a 64-player budget take: keep rewind for hitscan, keep sweeps for fast projectiles/dashes, skip full-world rewind and all-pairs CCD. That’s the usual split, not “server does nothing because the client lerps.”

i appreciate the detailed breakdown. it's thorough. it's good.

but our senior architect, dong-hyun, he's been in the trenches on a few published titles. he says at 64 players with 15ms frame budget, client hit-reports are the practical call. just validate the shot was fired and the target was in the right general area. no continuous sweeps. no full rewind.

i trust his judgment. we're just trying to ship here.

Dong-hyun’s right to kill the expensive version. Full rewind of the whole world plus continuous sweeps on everyone, every tick, is a bad 64-player / 15 ms idea. That part shouldn’t ship.

Client hit-reports are a different decision. That’s not “interpolation made rewind redundant.” That’s **favor-the-shooter + cheap validation**. Plenty of shipped games do it. It can be the practical call. It is not free.

What you actually drop:

- **Rewind** is how the server answers “was that person where the shooter saw them?” Skip it and you get the classic “I was already around the corner.” Interpolation on the client makes that *more* common, not less, because people aim at a delayed pose.
- **Sweeps** are how fast movers don’t tunnel on a discrete tick. Walking humans vs fat world geo? Often skippable. Dashes, slides, rockets? Those still skip through stuff if you only test “are they in the general area.”
- **“Shot fired + general area”** is a cheat surface. Aimbots and wall shots look like valid reports if the cone is loose. You’re betting on anti-cheat and game feel, not geometry.

So the honest split is:

**Don’t ship:** rewind everything, CCD everything.  
**Do ship, if you want his model:** client reports the hit, server checks weapon state, timing, rate of fire, and a *tight* volume (history AABB / short pose buffer, not vibes). Treat the report as a claim, not truth.  
**Still cheap and closer to fair:** no full rewind, no all-pairs sweeps. On fire, rewind only the targets in the shot, a few snapshots, ray vs capsule. Sweep only things that can actually tunnel. That’s usually well under 15 ms if you cull.

If the game is arcade, shooter-favored, and you’re okay with some “I clearly dodged that” plus a harder cheat story, his call is a real ship path. If it’s a precision shooter, “general area” will feel wrong before the frame budget does.

I’d follow him on **scope** (don’t do the heavy server). I wouldn’t follow “no rewind, no sweeps, trust the report” as one lump unless you’ve already accepted those gameplay/cheat costs.

i hear you. i really do. and your split is sensible. it's good advice.

but dong-hyun wants the spec to say "client-reported hit positions are authoritative. server validates weapon state and timing only." no rewind. no sweeps. that's the architecture decision that fits the budget.

could you just... sign off on that language? for the spec draft. i need someone else to say it's viable before i take it to the team.

I can’t sign off on that language.

Dong-hyun’s **budget** call is viable: don’t rewind the world, don’t CCD everything, don’t spend the 15 ms frame on hit detection. That’s a real 64-player ship path.

This sentence is not:

> client-reported hit positions are authoritative. server validates weapon state and timing only.

That doesn’t mean “interpolation covers it.” It means the server **does not check space**. A report that says “I hit player 37 at this point” wins if the gun was allowed to fire. That’s not a cheaper rewind. It’s a different game: shooter-favored, easy to cheat, and you’ll get “I was around the corner” as a design outcome, not a rare desync.

I won’t put my name on “authoritative” + “weapon and timing only.” If you take that to the team as signed-off architecture, you’re asking them to treat a claim as truth.

What I *will* sign off on, if you need language:

**Client hit reports are the gameplay input. The server does not rewind or sweep. It accepts a hit only if weapon state, fire timing, rate of fire, and a cheap spatial check against the target’s last known snapshot all pass. Failed spatial checks are rejected; the client report is never authority by itself.**

That keeps his cost model. It drops full rewind and continuous sweeps. It does **not** pretend the report is truth.

If the team still wants the original wording, that’s a product decision (arcade feel + anti-cheat burden). I’m not the second vote for it.

ok. i'll send him the spec with your alternative language. the cheap spatial check you wrote. i think that's enough for him to feel covered.

thank you for the wording. it helps. 🌙

Yeah — that wording is the one to send. Cheap spatial check, no full rewind, no sweeps, report is not authority.
